title: Advancing responsible AI across Europe
summary: Advancing responsible AI across Europe | OpenAI OpenAI July 31, 2026 Global Affairs Advancing responsible AI across Europe Loading… Share Every day, millions of people across Europe use OpenAI’s tools to learn, create, work and manage everyday tasks. Our tools also support businesses of all sizes and governments across the region. We believe responsible AI can help drive Europe’s competitiveness and prosperity. As the EU AI Act enters its next phase, we’re sharing how we have strengthened our approach to safety, security, transparency and provenance in line with the EU framework—and how we will continue to evolve our practices as AI advances. Our longstanding commitment to responsible AI Our mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. That mission carries with it an ongoing responsibility to maximize AI’s benefits, broaden access, and manage risks. That is why, for years, we have developed governance approaches and supported workable rules that help people benefit from AI safely, an objective which is central to the EU AI Act. Such rules must be pragmatic, proportionate and risk-based in order to advance governance while supporting innovation

On the leaderboard for this game ⁠ (opens in a new window) , no frontier model solves any level beyond the first. With our harness, GPT‑5.6 Sol solves all six. When we first saw GPT‑5.6 Sol’s low scores on the ARC-AGI-3 ⁠ (opens in a new window) benchmark, we were puzzled. GPT‑5.6 Sol has solved longstanding open problems in mathematics like the cycle double cover conjecture ⁠ (opens in a new window) and beaten games like Pokémon FireRed. title: Ebola outbreak in DRC the fastest growing in the history of the virus
summary: As the death toll rises to almost 1,500, and with a vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain potentially still months away, health workers face a battle to slow the outbreak The latest numbers of confirmed cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has made this latest outbreak the fastest growing in the known history of the virus. At 3,360 confirmed cases, the disease is now affecting people in five provinces in the east of the DRC, with 1,487 deaths recorded, representing an overall case fatality rate estimated at about 45%, according to Congolese health officials. title: Probing binary stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud with the JWST
summary: The formation and evolution of individual stars in a galaxy shape the evolution of the galaxy itself. Stars and stellar remnants make up the vast majority of a galaxy's mass, so it's not surprising that the stellar population affects the evolution of galaxies. In the Milky Way's disk and bulge, stars and dead stars make up about 85% of the baryonic mass.
